title: Operational SLO playbook for multi-variant model fallbacks and burst latency budgets
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: We need a concise, operational SLO playbook that prescribes exact latency targets, error budgets, and progressive rollout gates for scenarios where the serving runtime must fall back to cheaper/compatible model variants or cross-region capacity. Current SLO docs define broad targets but lack procedural gates for burst events, model-variant degradation, and automated rollback thresholds. This ticket scopes the PRD-level acceptance criteria and handoff artifacts for engineering and SRE to implement automated gating in the Console and runtime routing layer.
goals: 1) Define latency and availability SLOs by workload class (interactive chat, streaming, embeddings) with explicit percentile targets for steady-state and burst windows. 2) Specify error-budget consumption thresholds and automated actions (throttle, downgrade model variant, region failover) for progressive rollouts. 3) Produce a rollout gating matrix and implementation checklist for Console UI and runtime policy enforcement. 4) Define acceptance tests, monitoring dashboards, and runbook steps for SRE.
scope: In-scope: latency SLO definitions (p50/p90/p95/p99), burst window policies (1m/5m/1h rate), error-budget burn rules, canary % progression with automated guard rails, rollback triggers, and required metrics/events. Out-of-scope: billing changes, long-term contracts with customers, and on-prem install processes beyond API contract changes.
requirements_clarifications:
- Latency targets should be defined per workload class and per deployment tier (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).
- Burst windows must include both transient (1m) and short-term sustained (1h) definitions with separate thresholds.
- Rollout gate automation must be pluggable into existing Console rollout pipelines (canary -> 10% -> 33% -> 66% -> 100%).
- Fallback behavior: prefer model-variant downgrade (same architecture quantized) before cross-region failover to avoid higher egress/latency costs.
- All automated actions must emit audit events and be reversible by SRE/PM within Console.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Documented SLO matrix with numeric targets for chat (interactive) and embedding workloads across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
2) A gating matrix that ties specific error-budget burn rates and p95 degradation windows to concrete automated actions (hold, expand canary, rollback, downgrade variant).
3) Console changes that surface a canary progress UI and allow manual override; unit tests for gating logic and end-to-end test harness in staging.
4) Dashboards in Grafana that show SLOs, burn rates, canary status, and recent fallback events.
5) Runbook with step-by-step instructions for human intervention and postmortem template.
6) Two chaos/soak tests completed in staging demonstrating automated downgrade and rollback behavior with recorded metrics and incident review notes.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Decision: Use model-variant downgrade as first automated mitigation (favored for cost predictability) unless variant degrades quality beyond thresholds; cross-region failover reserved for severe capacity loss.
- Tradeoff: Aggressive automated rollbacks reduce customer exposure but increase risk of false positives; mitigated by requiring sustained threshold over 5m for critical rollbacks.
- Decision: For Private deployments, automated rollbacks are advisory by default; escalate to SRE with explicit customer opt-in for automatic actions.
implementation_notes:
- Engineering will need runtime hooks to emit per-request model-variant metadata and to support forced routing to a specific variant.
- Console: add 'SLO Gate' section to rollout UI with configurable thresholds and preview of audit events.
- Observability: new metrics: slo.p95.latency.{workload}.{tier}, slo.error_budget.remaining.{team}, rollout.canary_progress, fallback.events.count.
- Testing: create synthetic workload generator for chat and embedding patterns to validate burst policies.
